successCriteria.description: src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts exports a module-local constant named exactly LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE whose value is exactly the string 'leave_request' (case-sensitive), and it is not declared or re-exported anywhere under src/shared/.

Every audit entityType written by the leave write path (create, submit, approve, reject, cancel) in src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts is the LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE constant; no bare 'leave_request' string literal remains as an audit entityType argument in that file.

ILeaveService declares getHistory(actor: LeaveActor, requestId: string): Promise<AuditLog[]> and LeaveService implements it, with AuditLog imported from the audit module's public entry point (../audit) — no leave-owned projection or history-entry type is declared.

getHistory resolves visibility by calling the existing this.getById(actor, requestId) before any audit read, and returns the result of this.auditService.getByEntity(LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, requestId) unchanged (same array, same order, no re-sort, no mapping).

getHistory is read-only: it opens no transaction (no uow.withTransaction call), forwards no PoolClient, and performs no write; a visible request with zero matching audit rows resolves to an empty array rather than a thrown NotFoundError.

The project still typechecks and the existing Jest suites pass: the new ILeaveService member does not break the existing leave service/routes test doubles, and no test file under tests/ is modified by this phase.

constraints: LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE lives in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts only. It must NOT be promoted to src/shared/types/, must NOT be re-declared in leave.service.ts, and the audit module must never import or reference it (the audit module stays keyed generically on (entityType, entityId)).

getHistory must not re-express, duplicate, or branch on the leave visibility rule. It must not import or compare EmployeeRole, must not catch, wrap, or translate the NotFoundError thrown by getById, and must not produce a ForbiddenError. HARNESS.json declares EmployeeRole an owned decision of the leave and web-leave modules.

getHistory must not open a transaction, must not accept or forward a PoolClient, and must not write anything (no audit record, no notification, no repository mutation). The service keeps its existing injected collaborators; no new constructor dependency is added.

No leave-owned history type may be introduced: the audit module's AuditLog entity is the return/wire shape. Do not declare a LeaveHistoryEntry, AuditTrail, or similar projection in the leave module, and do not map or re-shape the returned entries.
Ordering is owned by the audit repository's SQL (occurred_at ASC, id ASC). getHistory must not re-sort, reverse, filter, paginate, or cap the returned array.

Scope is limited to src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts and src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts. No route, no controller, no test file, no migration, no schema/index change, and no change to src/modules/audit/ or src/shared/ in this phase.

Strict TypeScript: no `any` (use unknown with type guards), no implicit any, strict null checks. The audit module is imported only through its public entry point (../audit), never from its internal files.
outOfScope: The HTTP surface — the GET /leaves/:id/history route handler, actor resolution, and error serialization (Phase 3).
All tests for the trail read path — entity-query ordering/tie-break, endpoint visibility, byte-identical 404, empty-history, and response-field assertions (Phase 4).
Any change to the audit module's findByEntity/getByEntity, the audit_logs table, its (entity_type, entity_id) index, or the before_state/after_state serialization (Phase 1, already delivered).
Pagination, result caps, date/action filtering, redaction of beforeState/afterState or actorId, and any index extension — all recorded as open questions in the feature's architecture section.
Changing the GP-008 reversal semantics or giving a reversal row a trail of its own; the reversal's CANCEL entry stays keyed to the original request id.

ambiguities.description: Whether src/modules/leave/index.ts should also re-export LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE. The intent names only leave.model.ts and leave.service.ts, and no consumer outside the leave module needs the constant (the Phase 3 route serializes AuditLog entries and never references the literal).
options: Declare and export it from leave.model.ts only; leave index.ts unchanged (matches the stated file list)
Also re-export it from src/modules/leave/index.ts as part of the module's public surface

ambiguities.description: Scope of the literal substitution: the intent says replace bare 'leave_request' used as an audit entityType. leave.service.ts also passes 'leave_request' as the notification `type` and `relatedEntityType` (approve/reject/cancel), which are a different concern from the audit discriminator.
options: Substitute only the audit entityType arguments; leave the notification type/relatedEntityType literals untouched (matches the intent's wording)
Substitute every 'leave_request' literal in the file, including the notification ones

ambiguities.description: .gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json declares an `AuditTrail` read model (entityType, entityId, entries, entryCount) as a domain entity, while the intent and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's binding rule 10 require getHistory to return the audit-owned AuditLog[] directly with no leave-owned projection. The reconciled entity is a conceptual read model, not a required return type.
options: Return AuditLog[] as the intent and ARCHITECTURE.md binding rule 10 require; treat AuditTrail as a conceptual name only (no type is declared)
Introduce an AuditTrail wrapper type carrying entries/entryCount — contradicts the intent's explicit 'do NOT declare a leave-owned projection'

entityInvariants.invariant: A single, immutable, module-local discriminator with the exact value 'leave_request'. It is the one home for the literal: the leave write path and the leave history read both reference it, so writer and reader can never disagree. It is not a domain entity, has no lifecycle, and is never promoted to shared types or imported by the audit module.

Unchanged and immutable: an entry is written exactly once, inside the unit of work of the operation it describes, and is never updated, deleted, or re-recorded. This phase only reads it. Its shape is the wire shape for history — no field is added, renamed, dropped, or projected away.

entityInvariants.entity: LeaveRequest (leave module, lifecycle DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED)
entityInvariants.invariant: Unchanged by this phase — no state added, removed, or altered, and no field changed. A GP-008 reversal row is born CANCELLED, is terminal and inert, and has no audit trail of its own; its CANCEL entry is keyed to the ORIGINAL request id, so a trail read for the reversal id legitimately yields an empty array.

entityInvariants.entity: Audit trail of one leave request (read outcome, not a persisted entity)
entityInvariants.invariant: Identified by the PAIR (entityType, entityId), never by entityId alone. Two outcomes only: EMPTY (the request exists and is visible but no entry matches — a successful empty array, never an error) and POPULATED (one or more entries, oldest first). There is no partial or error state; a failed read throws rather than returning a partial trail.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authorization is delegated entirely to the existing LeaveService.getById(actor, requestId), called first and allowed to throw. ADMIN sees any request; MANAGER sees own plus direct reports (one level); anyone else sees only own. A caller who may not see the request receives the SAME NotFoundError (404, code NOT_FOUND) as a nonexistent id — never 403, never 401, never an empty array. No EmployeeRole branch and no role guard in this method.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Propagates getById's NotFoundError unchanged (no catch, no wrap, no translation). An empty audit result is a success returning [], never a NotFoundError. A malformed entityType/entityId reaching the audit service surfaces as ValidationError (400) from AuditService.getByEntity. No ConflictError is produced.

interfaceConstraints.operation: LeaveService.getHistory read semantics (transaction and client boundary)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only: opens no unit of work, takes and forwards no PoolClient, and writes nothing. It calls this.auditService.getByEntity(LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, requestId) with exactly two arguments and returns the array verbatim — same order, no re-sort, no mapping, no filtering, no cap.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Call the existing getByEntity with exactly the built signature `getByEntity(entityType: string, entityId: string): Promise<AuditLog[]>` — two arguments, no PoolClient. Do not add a client parameter or assume one exists.

Import AuditLog from the audit module's public entry point (`../audit`), which already exports it. Do not import from audit.model.ts or any other audit-internal file, and do not re-declare the type in leave.

getHistory must call the EXISTING getById(actor, requestId) implementation in this same class (the sole expression of the visibility rule) rather than re-deriving visibility from the repository or the employee service.

The audit entityType argument in create/submit/approve/reject/cancel must be replaced with LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, matching the value the history read passes. The notification `type`/`relatedEntityType` literals are a different concern and are not part of this substitution.

Declare LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE in this file alongside LeaveRequest/CreateLeaveRequestInput, following the module's existing export style, and export it so leave.service.ts imports it from './leave.model'.

Follow the existing ILeaveService declaration style: the new member is declared on the interface before the implementation, and LeaveService continues to `implements ILeaveService` so the interface and class stay in lockstep.

integrationPoints.why: The only read path for a trail; getHistory delegates to it with the two-argument signature and returns its array verbatim.
The single owner of the leave visibility rule; getHistory calls it first and lets its NotFoundError propagate, which is what makes invisible and nonexistent ids indistinguishable.
The return type of getHistory and the wire shape of a history entry; no leave-owned projection is introduced.
They construct LeaveService and cast to ILeaveService; adding an interface member must not break their typecheck. They are not modified in this phase.
